pr_title: Add tests for exotic external tar asset archives, fix some more corner case bugs
pr_body:
Addresses https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/74316 (excludes libarchive, which were not added as assets)

src changes:
- Remove unused `_readFirstEntry` field in `TarReader`.
- Add `processDataBlock` bool argument to `TryGetNextHeader` so that in the case of Pax, we don't read the data block until after we process the extended attributes, in case `size` is encountered among them and we override the original value.
- Throw more clearly when encountering a sparse entry. We won't support it for 7.0.
- Throw when encountering a size field > 0 in entries where data is not expected.
- When copying data, make sure that the freshly created memory stream is rewinded so that the user's first call of `DataStream` returns a stream positioned in the first byte, instead of the last byte.
- For octal fields, trim leading nulls and whitespaces. We already trim trailing nulls and whitespaces. @am11 https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/74358 my changes would conflict a lot with yours. I kept the change as simple and clear as possible, and only confined it to those two characters.

test changes:
- Cover all the new external exotic assets, with added explanations for those that had to be special cased.
- Make sure to test copyData as much as possible, both in uncompressed and gzipped archives.
- Added the copyData argument to the recently added tests in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/74396 cc @Jozkee .
- Sync and async.

What was the reason of handling it here when the other PR is up?

Is this the only case where this PR make us stricter than before? We're confident this isn't a real world case?

> Is this the only case where this PR make us stricter than before? We're confident this isn't a real world case?

Good question. I only encountered this problem in one of the archives, in a fifo entry, which is an entry type in which the data section is unexpected.

The code was already _not_ expecting data for those kinds of entries, but it would keep running until it tried to retrieve the next entry, and would encounter malformed data, because the position pointer would be offset (the pointer was not advancing beyond the unexpected data and its padding).

So I'd rather throw early than unexpectedly throw FormatException later, which would confuse the user.

This is the only case that would make us stricter, among these changes.

> Can you also check how we fare against the libarchive ones now?

Yes, I can do that next. We don't yet have them in runtime-assets, so I am not sure I'll have time to include it in this PR or in RC1.

Certainly the “there are two headers saying the same thing” exception is an intentional failure on our part that I’m not sure we should change.

One thing to keep in mind is TAR files are generally not created by humans (except gnarly test cases), so there’s not a lot of reason to be lax when reading. (Many, if not most (or even all), security bugs are related to ambiguity from lax reads.) Working around tool quirks (e.g. vendor X writes time stamps that get emitted with “.0” on the end and everyone else wrote them as an integer) is different than duplicate headers and other “okay, human, you’re trying to trick me” states.

Agreed about being excessively lax. As you point out, these test cases are not necessarily representative of customer inputs. We don't have good data. But if more than one of the other major tools accepts a file, I'd suggest we'd need to have a reason to not accept it. If only one does - perhaps doesn't matter.

Yes, these are mostly the corner cases and highly implementation-dependent. e.g. for `tar-rs/tests/archives/spaces.tar` that has spaces in octal valued headers, we noticed these differences in implementations:
* Rust, GNU tar and busybox: ignore leading and trailing nulls and whitespaces in octal valued headers (call`strtoull`)
* .NET: ignores only the trailing whitespaces and nulls
* libarchive: ignores leading and trailing nulls, whitespaces and any other non-octal character

Thank you so much @am11 for your help.

All the exceptions are expected from our library:

- `System.NotSupportedException: Entry type 'SparseFile' not supported.` - Expected. We aren't adding support for SparseFiles in 7.0 yet.
- `System.FormatException: The entry './PaxHeaders.38659/sparse' has a duplicate extended attribute.` - There is no reason to have two adjacent extended attributes. That's a bug in whatever tool created such archive. Not sure why libarchive allows this.
- `System.FormatException: The value of the size field for the current entry of type 'HardLink' is beyond the expected length.` Hardlinks are supposed to be links, they aren't supposed to have content. So their size should be zero.
- `System.FormatException: A POSIX format was expected (Ustar or PAX), but could not be reliably determined for entry 'commons-logging-1.2/NOTICE.txt'.` - Seems whatever tool generated this entry has a bug and is mixing the spec rules for GNU and PAX entries. The magic and the version are different in those two formats.

[This doc](https://manpages.debian.org/testing/libarchive-dev/tar.5.en.html) suggests that there is also a constraint on length of octal digits (six, seven, eleven depending on format, when it was implementation -- pre/post POSIX 1988 standard and the platform). We don't check for length at all, so we _are_ lenient as-is. Following what libarchive does for the octal (find first octal digit in header, read until the first non-octal digit or end of buffer), it won't be setting new precedence. Our `TarWriter` produces clean headers (octal followed by null), reader can be permissive.

Hey @mthalman I just ran into the unable to parse number issue as well using .NET's http client

Apparently the stream is being gziped twice I got a clue from here: https://github.com/icsharpcode/SharpZipLib/issues/514

In my case I was doing a similar thing:

```fsharp
task {
  use! str = http.GetStreamAsync url
  // System.IO.InvalidDataException: Unable To Parse Number
  TarFile.ExtractToDirectory(source, output, false)
}
```
Wrapping the stream from the http client made it work
```fsharp
task {
  use! str = http.GetStreamAsync url
  // It works
  use outer = new GZipStream(source, CompressionMode.Decompress)
  TarFile.ExtractToDirectory(outer, output, false)
}
```

It might be worth checking if it is a similar issue :)

Edit:

I'm not sure if this was a particular case of the .NET's HttpClient or a gzip gzip from node themselves I just know wrapping it made it work 😅
